title: Daily Debrief — Monday Nov 9, 2026
html:
Oil blinked, and SPY got its floor back.

Here's what I'm seeing. Oil slid on hopes of a deal with Iran, the AI trade bounced, and SPY jumped 2.4% back above the line we've been watching. Tomorrow's inflation report decides if it sticks.

Links: SPY AAPL TSLA XOM NOW DELL PLTR Watchlist Options Playbook Fed Tracker Federal Reserve Fibonacci Playbook

The one thing

SPY closed back above $745, the old floor. Tomorrow's 8:30 a.m. inflation report (CPI) decides if that holds. Hold $745 and the selloff was a scare; lose it and today was just a bounce.

SPY closed at $752.69, up 2.4%. The S&P 500 rose 2.35% to 7,549.94, the Dow added 1,104 points and small caps led (+3.2%). The VIX, the market's fear gauge, fell 22% to about 20.

What drove it: oil fell about 4% (December crude near $87) after President Trump said new strikes on Iran are unlikely while talks continue. Cheaper oil helps airlines and eases inflation worries, so travel and tech both rallied. AMD jumped 13% on an analyst upgrade.

The exception was Nvidia, down 4.3% after its board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. SPY's rally also stalled at $755.42, just under the next Fib ceiling at $757.

The market in one picture: SPY

Last week SPY lost its floor at $744–745 (the 23.6% retracement of the big March–October run). Today it closed back above it. Above us, the drop from the October record has its own Fib levels: the 50% at $757.17 stopped today's high, and the 61.8% at $762.94 sits with the 20- and 50-day averages at $762–765. Levels that bunch together like that are called confluence, and they matter more than a single line.

SPY ladder

  • Oct 6 record high: $781.62

How I read it: a pullback inside an uptrend that just got its floor back. What changes my view: a close above $757, then $765, says the selloff is over (and the SPY call idea is on). A close back below $745 after CPI says today was only a bounce; below $722 the uptrend breaks.

Earnings are Nov 17, and puts are EXPENSIVE: the Dec $168 put prices in 57% volatility while the stock has been moving 41% (ratio 1.38, earnings inside). Stand aside until after the report.

XOM — Wait

Down 0.7% to $164.73. The high, $165.55, failed under your 2.0 extension ($166.89) for the third day in a row, so the old support is acting as resistance. Oil slid again. Next support is your 1.618 at $159.09.

Lesson of the day: Why a winning call can outgrow the budget: delta

Delta is how much an option's price moves when the stock moves $1. A delta of 0.27 means the option gains about 27 cents per share (that's $27 per contract) for every $1 the stock rises. As the stock moves toward the strike, delta grows, so the option speeds up. That's the leverage that makes calls pay, and it works the same way in reverse.

  • SPY Dec $765 call, Friday: $638 (delta 0.27 · SPY $735.29)
  • Same call, today: $1,029 (delta 0.41 · SPY $752.69)

SPY rose 2.4%, and this call rose 61%. Its delta went from 0.27 to 0.41, so it now moves about $41 per contract for each $1 in SPY. The rally pushed it over the $800 limit before CPI gave us the green light. That's fine: the rule to wait for CPI was right, and we simply move up one notch to the $775 call ($611, delta 0.30). A lower delta costs less but needs a bigger move, so stay at or above 0.20.

Why: your tested edge, an uptrend with RSI under 40, after a bounce off the golden pocket. Enter: a move above $172.23. Exit: a close below $158. Targets: $182.77, then $185.5–190. Delta 0.40. Setup: uptrend + RSI<40.

Why: SPY took back its old floor. Enter: only if SPY holds above $745 after Tuesday's CPI. Exit: below $732. Targets: $757, then $762–765. Delta 0.30. Replaces the $765 call, now $1,029. Setup: reclaim of old floor.

OI 17,387 · vol 30,078 · bid/ask $6.08/$6.14

BA Dec 18 $170 put — $580 most you can lose — IV 33% vs moves 36% → FAIR

Why: a true downtrend leaning on its October low. Enter: a break below $165, or a failed rally into $179–181.5. Exit: a close above $185. Targets: $156.34, then $147.61. Delta −0.41. Setup: breakdown / failed rally.

OI 4,123 · vol 228 · bid/ask $5.60/$6.00

Cheap or expensive compares the option's built-in guess of movement (implied volatility, IV) with how much the stock has really moved over the last 60 days. All three are FAIR: you're paying about the going rate for the movement.

Scorecard: 1 closed, 1-0, +$527.50 · 2 open (+$195 on paper) · 3 watching · early read

Skip this: NVDA puts into the Nov 17 earnings (EXPENSIVE, ratio 1.38). DELL and SMH puts: the near-money ones cost $1,500+ and the ones under $800 are lottery tickets. Chasing another DAL call with RSI at 67. RCL and HLT calls: their options trade too thinly (RCL Dec $370 call: 12 contracts today).

Homework

  1. PLTR: mark $172.23 on the daily chart. Tomorrow, does the candle close above it, or poke through and fall back (a wick)?
  2. SPY: mark $745 and $757. After CPI at 8:30, note which one price reaches first, and whether the first hour's move holds into the close.

If CPI comes in hot and SPY opens at $740, under the line, what happens to the SPY idea, and what would you do with your open DAL call?

  • DAL — price crosses above $95.18 → target 2, take profits
  • SPY — price crosses below $745.00 → the reclaim failed, SPY call idea on hold

An alert means look now, not buy now.

Fib in action: The golden pocket: where PLTR's pullback stopped (Fibonacci Playbook)

Most healthy pullbacks end between the 50% and 61.8% retracements of the run before them. Traders call that band the golden pocket.

PLTR's run: A = the Jun 25 low $106.37, B = the Oct 12 high $212.94 (the lowest low and highest high of the move), a $106.57 rise. 50%: $212.94 − $106.57 × 0.5 = $159.65. 61.8%: $212.94 − $106.57 × 0.618 = $147.08.

Last Thursday's drop bottomed at $152.60, inside the pocket and on the 200-day. Friday closed back above 50%, and today PLTR ran to $169.20. For a trade: the entry comes on strength (above the 38.2% at $172.23), the stop goes just under the 50% at $158, and the 23.6% ($187.79) is the target that points to the $180 strike.

Try it yourself: on DAL, draw from the Oct 20 low $74.14 to today's high $92.49. Where is its golden pocket, and where does the $83 stop sit?
